decisive_items: heterozygous mutation (c.754G>A, p.A252T) in the HTRA1 gene
lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities (WMH)
lobe-dominant distribution of multiple cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) and relatively fewer CMBs in deep regions
response.rationale: The heterozygous HTRA1 mutation directly establishes HTRA1-related hereditary cerebral small vessel disease; the MRI findings and family history of stroke/cognitive decline are consistent. CADASIL would require NOTCH3, and CAA is unlikely at age 44 with a confirmed HTRA1 mutation.

rejected.why: Lobar cerebral microbleeds can suggest CAA, but the finding of a pathogenic HTRA1 mutation and younger age make HTRA1-related disease more likely; no amyloid-specific evidence is present.
CADASIL can cause lacunar infarctions and white matter hyperintensities, but it is caused by NOTCH3 mutations; the supplied genetic finding is HTRA1, not NOTCH3.
